plan.english: Let him go below, into the darkness.

notes: The darkness as the place the dead go to (West 2007 ch. 10, 'lower darkness'): Ved. ádharaṃ gamayā támaḥ 'make him go to the lower darkness' (RV 10.152.4) and Lucr. 1.115 an tenebras Orci uisat 'or whether (the soul) visits the darkness of Orcus' (both checked): darkness as the goal of a verb of going. Secure is *témHos at formation level: Lat. tenebrae < *temas-rā is a derivative of the s-stem that Ved. támas- continues. Round 2: 'below' (*Hn̥dʰér) is no longer claimed: the 'lower' adjective is Vedic ádhara- and Latin infernus only in Aen. 7.325 (West; not in the local corpora), and the lexicon has only the adverb, so it is interpolated; Catullus 3.13–14, Aen. 7.325 and Lucr. 3.628 (infernae animae, not darkness) are support. The verb: Ved. gamaya is a causative ('make him go'), Lucretius has uiso: a plain 3sg imperative of *gʷem- is interpolated.

plan.english: The Twin's two dogs guard the path.

notes: The dog(s) guarding the way to the dead (West 2007 ch. 10 'Beware of the Dog'): Yama's two dogs (dual śvā́nau, 'path-guarding'), the two dogs of Vd. 13.9 (dual spāna) that guard the bridge, and the hound of Hades (Kerberos). Only *ḱwṓ is shared across branches. 'The Twin' (yemHós = Yama) is Vedic in this passage; Av. -pāna 'guarding' continues *peh₂- but is Indo-Iranian only; 'path' (Ved. pathi-) likewise. The dual follows Vedic and Avestan. The four-eyed (caturakṣá-, Av. caϑru.cašma-) and spotted (śabála-, perhaps = Κέρβερος) epithets have no usable lexeme.

plan.english: You put them down to sleep.

notes: Killing as 'putting to sleep' with the causative *swop-éye-: Ved. (ní) svāpaya- of Indra's foes (West 2007 ch. 10 lists RV 1.121.11, 4.30.21, 7.19.4, 9.97.54), OE swebban 'put to sleep, kill' (Beowulf 680 in the local Harrison–Sharp text; āswefede 'put to sleep by swords' 567), Lat. sōpīre (Lucr. 3.904 leto sopitus 'put to sleep by death'). Past (imperfect) as in Ved. ásvāpayaḥ, 2sg addressed to the god. ní 'down' and the pronoun object are Vedic-only, interpolated.

The slain lie (Watkins 1995 ch. 53, SLAY ... LIE): *gʷʰn̥tó- + *ḱey- middle. Round 2: rebuilt as the 3rd plural, which is what the Indo-Iranian passages have: Av. yaɱi sōire ... jata 'where (the Mithra-deceivers) lie slain' (Yt. 10.80 = CAB YtMihr21.3g–h) and Ved. yátra hatā́ḥ amítrāḥ ... áśeran 'where the slain enemies lay' (RV 1.133.1, a locus not used by the other slain-lie lines), with Hekabe's πρόσφατος ... κεῖσαι 'newly slain you lie' (Il. 24.757–758) as the Greek. Present as in Avestan and Greek (Vedic imperfect). The round-1 line's 'now' rested on OE nū beside ligeð (*legʰ-), which is dropped. The plural predicate adjective has no noun (Ved. amítra- 'enemy' is not cognate). Still close in content to dragon-slaying-006 and cattle-raid-002 (same formula, other person and number); all loci checked locally. Engine limit: it gives the regular 3pl middle ḱéyn̥tor; the daughters' 3pl (Av. sōire, Ved. áśeran, śére) continue the archaic r-ending (*-ro(y)), which the engine does not build.

Lying and sleep in one passage for the slain: Vṛtra 'lying' (ā-śáyāna-, *ḱey-) is put to sleep (siṣvapaḥ) by Indra's weapon; the slain Iphidamas 'lay down in the bronze sleep' (κοιμήσατο, a *ḱey- derivative, with ὕπνον = *supnós); the dead dragon 'lies, sleeps' (Beowulf). *supnós is the Greek ablaut form; Ved. svap- and OE swefan are root-level matches. Locative 'in sleep' is interpolated (Greek has a cognate accusative). Round 2: Beowulf is support only (licgan is *legʰ-, swefan a verb, not *supnós), so the line stands on Vedic and Greek, both root-level for 'lie' (Gk κοιμάω is a derivative of *ḱey-) and Ved. svap- root-level for *supnós; cf. RV 2.15.9 svápnena 'with sleep' in a slaying (a -no- noun like ὕπνος, other ablaut grade).

Watkins 1995 (nectar as *neḱ-tr̥h₂- 'overcoming death'): Ved. áti tarāṇi mṛtyúm 'may I cross beyond death' (subjunctive 1sg). Only *terh₂- is shared; the death noun is renewed (Ved. mṛtyú-, Gk νεκ-), so *mértis (Ved. mṛtí-, Lat. mors) is interpolated, as is *éti 'over' (= Ved. áti).

plan.english: Having crossed death, he has reached what is immortal.

notes: Watkins 1995: Īśā Up. 14 'having crossed death ... he attains the immortal' encodes both halves of Gk νέκταρ τε καὶ ἀμβροσίην: *neḱ-terh₂- 'overcoming death' and *n̥-mr̥-to- 'undying' (Ved. amṛ́tam, Gk ἀμβροσίη). *h₂neḱ- 'reach' (Ved. aśnute, present) is Vedic only and interpolated; the perfect 'has reached' renders the attained state. Death noun interpolated as in death-otherworld-006. Round 2: VS 40.14 is not in the local DCS (it has VSM 1–15 only); Il. 19.347 checked.

Crossing to the dead (West 2007 ch. 10): the Chinvat 'crossing' (pərətu- = *pértus, cf. Lat. portus) of the Gāthās and Vīdēvdād; Patroclus' shade begs burial 'that I may pass the gates of Hades' (περήσω). Root-level: Avestan has the noun, Greek the verb of *per- 'cross'. 1sg prospective follows the Greek future; Y. 46.10 is likewise Zarathustra's first-person promise. The figura (verb + cognate noun) is the projection's; neither passage has both words.

Dying as going to (join) the dead (West 2007 ch. 10): Hector 'thought to reach the dead and the house of Hades this day'; OIr techt do écaib 'going to the dead' (idiom, quoted from West). Gk νέκυς and OIr éc (< *n̥ḱu-) continue *néḱus. The verbs are not cognate (ἱκνέομαι, techt); *gʷem- 'come' is interpolated. Round 2: Od. 11.37 (νεκύων only) is support; OIr techt do écaib is quoted from West and not in the local corpora; Il. 15.251 checked.

Watkins 1995 'bring death': Gk φόνον φέρειν, ON banorð bera 'bear (someone's) death-word, cause his death'. φόνος is *gʷʰónos; ON bana- (bani 'slayer, death') is an n-stem of the same o-grade, a root-level match. Plural as in Il. 2.352; the dative of the victims is left out.

plan.english: The Twin died first of mortals.

notes: Yama, 'who died first of mortals' (AV 18.3.13) and chose death (RV 10.13.4); his Iranian counterpart Yima (Y. 9.4–5, where under his rule there was no death — the Avestan passage denies death in his reign, his fall follows in Yt. 19); ON Ymir is the cosmogonic Twin (West 2007 chs. 9–10). Only the name *yemHós 'twin' is shared beyond Indo-Iranian. The death verb and 'mortals' are Indo-Iranian only (Ved. mamā́ra, mártya-; Av. mərəϑiiu-, maṣ̌iia-) and interpolated; 'first' renders Ved. prathamá- with the lexicon's *pr̥h₂wós.

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. Watkins 1995 ch. 51 'be the death of' (*h₁es- + *gʷʰon-o-, be-the-death-of). Old Norse Hávamál 72 (FJ 1926 numbering) tunga es hǫfuðs bani 'the tongue is the head's bane' (es = er 'is'; checked in the FJ 1926 text). Greek Il. 16.144 (= 19.391) the ash spear φόνον ἔμμεναι ἡρώεσσιν 'to be death for heroes', Od. 11.444 οὐ σοί … φόνος ἔσσεται 'death will not be yours (from your wife)' (AGDT). Verb *h₁ésti: exact in Old Norse, root in the builder for Greek εἰμί (ἔμμεναι infinitive, ἔσσεται future). Noun: Greek φόνος = *gʷʰónos exact; ON bani is the n-stem *gʷʰon-en- 'slayer, bane', root level. Interpolated: the subject 'this' (the spear in Il. 16.144, the tongue in Hávamál), the dative 'for you' (from Od. 11.444; ON has a genitive), and the present tense (Hávamál present, Greek future and infinitive; the engine has no future). Support: Beo. 587 tō banan wurde 'became the bane (of your brothers)', with *wert- 'become' for *h₁es-. OE/ON 'at bana verða' is the same renewal.
